sources.title: #data-insights: invoice API traffic mix
sources.author: P10
sources.text: Ran the numbers on invoice API traffic since the bulk import launch. Writes are now 58% of requests, so it is no longer read-heavy. Caching reads will not move p95 much.

sources.title: Churn exit survey, Q3 summary
sources.author: P13
sources.text: Exit survey, 212 responses. Price is the top reason for only 14% of churned accounts; missing integrations (41%) and setup friction (27%) rank higher.

sources.title: Latency profile of the invoice API
sources.author: P11
sources.text: Profiling shows synchronous PDF rendering accounts for 61% of p95 latency.

sources.title: #payments: delivery failure breakdown
sources.author: P07
sources.text: Of last month's failed deliveries, 83% are provider-side bounces.

sources.title: Decision record D-101: Cache invoice reads in Redis
sources.author: P01
sources.text: Decision: Cache invoice reads in Redis. We are doing this because: Invoice API traffic is read-heavy, so caching reads cuts latency. Success means API p95 latency changes by -30% from its pre-launch level by 2026-04-20.

sources.title: #platform: cache invoice reads in redis
sources.author: P06
sources.text: Proposal thread for 'Cache invoice reads in Redis'. Agreed to go ahead; decision record to follow.
